name: Storm-0530
iocPatterns: Hidden HTML redirect codes in website content
Visual Basic (VBS) scripts used for execution
Obscured URLs on social media platforms
Malicious document lures for high-profile topics
keyCapabilities: Watering hole and social media lure exploitation
Automated script execution for system profiling
Data exfiltration and collection of PII
Hidden HTML redirection for traffic manipulation
Malicious link dissemination across public platforms
recommendedActions: Block known malicious domains and IPs associated with hidden redirect scripts.
Audit web content for unauthorized script injections or hidden HTML redirect code.
Filter and inspect outgoing traffic to identify connections to known ransomware C&C servers.
Implement advanced endpoint detection (EDR) focused on identifying multi-platform backdoors like Crutch or Kazuar.
Block the execution of unsigned VBS scripts in system directories.
Educate employees on the risks of clicking social media links in non-primary business contexts.
Conduct regular scans for known Turla-linked malware signatures across both Windows and Linux environments.
Implement strict application whitelisting to prevent the use of unauthorized common tools like Powellshell for persistence.
campaignsText: Storm-0530 shows a long operational history, with the Turla component active since roughly 1996. Notable historical campaigns include Operation Dust Storm (2010), the 'Epic Turla' campaign infiltrating over 45 countries in 2013, and the RUAG breach in 2014 targeting Swiss military interests. Recently, the group has been more frequently observed using the H0lyGh0st persona to target small businesses for ransomware-related economic gain.
description: Storm-0530 is a sophisticated North Korean threat actor that exhibits a dual operational profile: conducting high-level cyberespionage linked to Turla APT and pursuing financial motives through the H0lyGh0st ransomware campaign. The actor targets across a broad array of sectors including government, defense, and critical infrastructure, utilizing multi-platform backdoors and complex delivery techniques.
goals: Storm-0530 operates with a hybrid motive: high-level cyberespionage for strategic gain and financial extortion to bypass economic sanctions. Their goal is the theft of sensitive information from governmental and critical infrastructure sectors while simultaneously funding their operations through the H0lyGh0st ransomware campaign targeting smaller commercial entities.
